extracted.intended_audience: landscape painters, art students, and practicing artists studying rendering of foreground, rocks, soil, and water
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and critical guidance for painting landscape foregrounds (rocks, loose soil, banks, detached blocks) and water, emphasizing truthful observation, line, light-and-shade, geological logic, variety, and unity. Includes examples and anti-patterns drawn from older masters and Turner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct and sharp light-and-shade separate from local color
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark the distinct and sharp light and shade by which the form is explained, never confusing it with local color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care, firmness, and success in separating chiaroscuro from color are essential; Stanfield's foregrounds exemplify this. Use determined shadowing to explain fissures and form rather than letting local color obscure form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play of line to indicate stratification and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Vary the play of line to indicate the regularity of stratification and the underlying organization of rock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lines should be varied and instructive, showing stratification and cleavage; compare drawings that show stratification ascending in perspective (e.g., Ischia, Botallack Mine).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine, fractured brushwork for rocky surfaces (avoid broad daubs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid huge concave sweeps of the brush, daubing, or splashing; render rock foregrounds as brittle, splintery, with fissures explained by precise light and shade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every inch should feel tangible and chiselled; do not use broad, sweeping curves like Salvator's 'daubs'; treat each texture with small, incisive touches so the eye can 'stumble over the edges of them.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid monotonous repetition of identical lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure variety so 'not one line is like another' — avoid repeating the same curve or mark across the composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monotony (as in Salvator or Teniers' ground) creates unnatural continuity where the eye stops; make each line distinct to preserve natural irregularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural spontaneity in fragmenting and scattering of rock
rubrics_metrics.description: Render fragments as if they 'fell from under the hand'—splintered and scattered with freedom and facility, appearing true without apparent effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hard, laborious-looking execution is less convincing than work that suggests ease; emulate Harding's facility in giving fragments a freshly-broken look.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate, expressive rock coloration (avoid 'mud' or cold grays)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use rich, lichenous, and changeful warm tones and delicate weathered grays rather than muddy or cold grays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color must support the truth of rock; Harding is praised for his colorfulness compared to artists who verge on mud or coldness in gray.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study from nature, not mannerism
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not paint with a preconceived manner ('Pynize' everything); instead, study and be taught by nature directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent sketching without deep study leads to mannerism; draw specific natural examples (e.g., four trees from a turnpike-road) leaf for leaf to learn truth rather than rely on invented conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed rendering of loose earth and small-scale soil features
rubrics_metrics.description: Render steep banks and loose earth with undulating lines from rain descent, little ravines, ridges, chiselled contours, precipices above harder knots, jagged hanging fractures, and shadows that explain structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even small banks under three feet have rich, mountain-like organization. Shadows must be expressive of true structural relationships; treat these minor forms with the same seriousness as larger features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety and non-repetition in soil contours and curves
rubrics_metrics.description: Curves should be varied, not monotonous; avoid sweeping unbroken flows that repeat and let the eye 'leap' from one to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teniers' ground is faulted for monotonous repeating curves and lack of 'determined shadow' — introduce delicate angles and pauses to emulate natural touch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to minor parts distinguishes master from novice
rubrics_metrics.description: The real distinction between master and novice lies in rendering finer truths—delicate fissures, descending curves, and undulating shadows in mouldering soil with gentle, fine touch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic brush freedom and ordinary accuracy can be learned quickly; the master discovers and renders 'mysteries of invention and combination' that nature shows in trivial things.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not trust earth-drawing to chance or imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid inventing banks or substituting 'lumps of dough' for stones; even painters who observed nature (e.g., Cuyp) sometimes treated earth carelessly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw actual stones and formations from nature; invention without reference leads to childish or incompetent results (as in Claude's painted banks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified recession of ground; avoid artificial successive edges
rubrics_metrics.description: Portray receding ground as one united mass with modulations that are 'members, not divisions,' rather than a succession of fully edged promontories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artificially dividing banks into distinct promontories with maintained sharp edges makes the picture look constructed and prevents the eye's smooth progression (Claude criticized for this). Use subtle graduation so edges are briefly felt then lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infinite variety within unity (Turner's principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine infinite variety of detail with perfect unity so the eye is guided imperceptibly over round surfaces and cannot take the foreground by abrupt divisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid single edges; everywhere keep forms rounded and retiring so the viewer progresses without perceptible jumps — the eye should be able to travel 'a quarter of a mile into the picture.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate geological structure with surface weathering
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate strata directions, series of joints, fissures, and how weather/torrent modify these into convex surfaces and fractured edges, so the whole tells a geological history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show horizontal lines of strata, vertical fissures, rounded salient edges, inward angles with determined shadow and transparent reflex. Good drawing should allow a geologist to reason reliably about past and future phenomena at the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of chiaroscuro to model mass (hierarchy of shadows)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat the mass of rock like a portrait head: a principal broad light-and-shade structure with subsidiary, varying, fainter shades that never disturb the wholeness and grandeur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One deep marked shadow indicates greatest proximity, from which other shadows become fainter until lost in obscurity; maintain a consistent hierarchy of tones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Render local exceptions when dictated by specific action
rubrics_metrics.description: Where local forces (e.g., eddies, torrent vortices) produce concave curves or other departures from general rules, depict those exceptions exactly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turner's Llanthony example: eddies may cut vaults that interrupt universal convexity; masterly work applies general rules but attends to local deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individuality of repeated elements within subordinate unity
rubrics_metrics.description: In masses of debris or many rocks, give each block individual character and clear chiselling while preserving its subordinate role within the whole mass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every separate block should look studied and distinct (as if drawn from nature) yet not repeat a single line across the group; avoid homogeneous repetition in crowded foregrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make small details significant; elevate the minutiae
rubrics_metrics.description: The rank of a painter is seen in how he treats minutiae—by making small things great rather than ignoring them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an artist cannot make a bank sublime, he will make a mountain ridiculous; invest care and intellectual interest in small foreground features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foregrounds as sources of continual discovery and layered truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Compose foregrounds so that on repeated viewings the observer discovers new relations and truths; the parts should be so united that the eye is guided from stone to stone within a new system each time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turner's foregrounds teach different truths according to the viewer's approach; aim for abundance and depth so the picture rewards repeated study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic method for suggesting calm water (projection curves + highlights)
rubrics_metrics.description: To suggest ordinary calm water, observe careful curves of projection with a dark ground and break a little white over it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ordinary representation of calm or ordinary running water this simple method (used with judgment by Ruysdael) is often sufficient; but it is only the starting point for more complex reflective effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deeply observe and render reflections and what's beneath the surface
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not slur reflections or improvise; water often contains as much landscape as above it—trees, leaves, bottom stones, sky reflections—and these must be drawn as fully as the actual scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketch polluted or common ponds thoroughly: draw trees, shaking leaves, hazy sunlight passages, bottom stones, and sky reflections with delicate attention; the great painter 'sees beneath' and follows it even if it takes a day's work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conventional 'improvements' of water; follow visual truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Resist 'improving' nature by clearing or brightening water with coarse flashes of color; follow the complex, delicate, and often saddened reflections true to the scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many artists replace subtle polluted-water reflections with crude blues/greens/yellows; instead, strive for the refined, complex, and sombre passages that convey water's depth and character.
